chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi al-Kufi narrated that Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to me that al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated to me that Bakr ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, said: 'I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about al-Tawhid, and he said:'

'Whoever recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and believes in it has recognized al-Tawhid.' I said: 'How should we recite it?' He said: 'As the people recite it.' He added to it: 'Kadhalika Allahu Rabbi, Kadhalika Allahu Rabbi, Kadhalika Allahu Rabbi' - three times.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: al-Rida (title of Imam Musa al-Kadhim or his son depending on context, here referring to the Imam)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Say, He is Allah, the One)
key_terms.كَذَلِكَ اللَّهُ رَبِّي: Kadhalika Allahu Rabbi (Thus/So is Allah my Lord)

ai.seo_question: How does one recognize Divine Unity (Tawhid) according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) simplifies the complex theological concept of Tawhid by linking it directly to the recitation of Surah Ikhlas, emphasizing that sincere belief in its concise declaration of God's oneness is sufficient for recognition. The specific instruction to add 'Kadhalika Rabbi' three times highlights a devotional practice of personal affirmation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both textual fidelity and internalized conviction. This narration underscores the accessibility of core doctrine, bridging the gap between scholarly theological definitions and the spiritual experience of the common believer.
